attribution.note: Marcus directly endorses the assertion that Piltch replicated their results.

semantics.note: The normalisation faithfully captures a completed replication of the central image-generation finding, without asserting a legal determination of infringement.

contract.note: Reproducing recognizable characters through unnamed-character prompts fairly captures the central phenomenon. Identical outputs, universal success, and absence of prior contact are not required.

evidence.note: Piltch's contemporaneous firsthand report documents his own recognizable character outputs from generic prompts. Generic outputs from other services and inconsistent success do not defeat replication of the central phenomenon.

The dated caption identifies the original investigation's subject. It supplies comparison context, not independent proof of replication; the unavailable article body is unnecessary given e1's description.

reviews.rationale: Piltch reports personally generating recognizable characters from prompts omitting their names, including a prompt borrowed from Marcus and Southen. His report was published by the claimed date. Mixed results across services limit generality but do not undermine the stated replication.
